headline: Steady growth, expanding margins, and continued buybacks
summary_short: Revenue rose 21.9% y/y to $1,630M in Q1 FY2026 as Toast's Location count grew 22% to approximately 171,000; net income more than doubled y/y to $126M and Adjusted EBITDA rose 34.6% to $179M.
summary_long: Revenue grew 21.9% y/y to $1,630M, driven by more Locations (~171,000, +22% y/y) and product adoption across subscription and fintech solutions revenue. Costs of revenue rose 19% on higher fintech-solutions costs tied to GPV growth ($51.3B in the quarter, +22% y/y); operating expenses rose 11% on higher employee costs, partly offset by lower restructuring. Operating income rose to $110M and net income more than doubled y/y to $126M. Adjusted EBITDA rose 34.6% y/y to $179M and free cash flow rose to $115M from $69M. ARR reached $2,151M, up 26% y/y. Toast repurchased $327M of stock in the quarter, plus $51M more through May 6, under an expanded $500M buyback program; cash fell q/q mainly on those repurchases.

drivers.explanation: Revenue growth was driven by more Locations and continued product adoption; profitability scaled faster than revenue as 11% opex growth lagged 22% revenue growth, lifting operating income, net income, and Adjusted EBITDA.
Growth was primarily driven by higher subscription services and financial technology solutions revenue, tied to more Locations on the platform and continued product adoption.

Gross profit rose as revenue growth (22%) outpaced cost-of-revenue growth (19%); costs of revenue increased mainly on higher financial-technology-solutions costs tied to increased gross payment volume.
Operating expenses rose only 11% (higher employee-related costs, partly offset by lower restructuring expense) against 22% revenue growth, expanding operating income both q/q and y/y.
Net income growth tracks the operating-income gain; income tax expense rose to $5M from $2M but pretax income growth outpaced it. Not further explained in the release.
EPS growth combines the net income increase with a roughly flat weighted diluted share count (602M vs 603M a year ago).
This shard-sourced figure tracks the same revenue and cost drivers as operating income above; it is not the same measure as the company's own Adjusted EBITDA non-GAAP figure below.
Company-defined Adjusted EBITDA excludes stock-based compensation, D&A, interest, taxes, and other non-operating items; the 34.6% y/y rise reflects the same revenue and opex drivers cited above.
ARR growth reflects higher subscription and payments MRR components, driven by the same Location growth and product-adoption trends behind this quarter's revenue growth.
Cash fell mainly on $227M used in financing activities (primarily $323M of share repurchases), partly offset by $129M of operating cash flow, net of $75M used in investing activities.
Not directly explained in the release; the q/q decline likely reflects treasury-stock reductions from $327M of share repurchases during the quarter, partly offset by $126M of net income.
Diluted share count was roughly flat y/y (602M vs 603M) as ongoing share repurchases offset new share issuance from equity-plan settlements.
